title: Step 2: the risk profile picks a point
objectives: Give the conservative, moderate and aggressive illustrative mixes for a 7+ year goal.
Explain why these are teaching examples, not model portfolios.
body_md:
Within the horizon range, the client's risk profile picks the point.

## Illustrative mixes for a 7+ year goal

| Profile | Equity | Debt | Gold |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conservative | 30% | 60% | 10% |
| Moderate | 50% | 40% | 10% |
| Aggressive | 70% | 20% | 10% |

## What these are, and are not

They are teaching examples, not Fund Horizon model portfolios. Every client's mix is set after a proper risk profile, and the profile is re-run every two to three years or after a life event.

## The point of the three rows

Two clients with the same 20-year goal can legitimately hold 30% or 70% equity. The difference is not the goal; it is how much loss each can afford and live with. Getting that wrong is how a good mix gets abandoned in the first bad year.
example: Two clients, both retiring in 20 years. One has a stable government pension and a high tolerance: 70/20/10. The other has an irregular business income and low tolerance: 30/60/10. Same goal, different mixes.
say: Your risk profile picks the point inside the range for your horizon.
Two clients with the same goal can hold very different mixes, and both be right.
never: This is our model portfolio for everyone.
Aggressive is always better over 20 years.

talk_track.text: Step two: the client's risk profile picks a point within that range. For a goal seven or more years away, here are three teaching examples. Conservative: thirty percent equity, sixty percent debt, ten percent gold. Moderate: fifty, forty, ten. Aggressive: seventy, twenty, ten. These are teaching examples only, not Fund Horizon model portfolios.
